usageNotes: Use this to enable, disable, or tune the per-container firewall for an LXC guest on a remote PVE node via PDM. The firewall is inactive by default (enable=false); you must explicitly set enable=true for rules to take effect. Supply a digest from the current options read to guard against concurrent modifications — omitting it skips the conflict check.

examples.summary: Enable the container firewall with DROP default policies, DHCP allowed, and info-level inbound logging

tips: Firewall rules are silently ignored until enable=true is set — verify this flag if traffic is not being filtered as expected.
ipfilter=true on containers automatically populates ipset entries with the container's configured IP addresses, preventing IP spoofing without manual ipset management.
macfilter defaults to true; disabling it can allow MAC spoofing from within the container, so only disable for specific bridging or migration scenarios.
Use the delete array to revert individual settings to their defaults rather than overwriting the entire config — e.g., delete=["log_level_in"] to stop logging without touching other options.
ndp=true is required for IPv6 neighbor discovery to work in containers; disabling it will break IPv6 connectivity even when rules otherwise permit it.
